title: PADD: Path-Aligned Decompression Distillation for Non-Router Teacher to Guide MoE Student Learning
claim: A multi-stage training procedure combines initialization, online distillation, policy optimization and load balancing into one unified pipeline with feedback loops.
layout: 4 stage columns, left-to-right, dashed feedback loops across top and bottom
description: A wide four-column diagram with colored stage headers: blue for Stage I (initialize and warmup), cyan for Stage II (forward), pink for Stage III (backward) and yellow for Stage IV (parameter update). The left column shows neuron clustering of a dense teacher FFN into clusters C1 to CN. Below it, expert warmup initializes a frozen router and student experts, with warmup losses L_init, L_LM and L_KD. The middle columns hold rounded boxes joined by solid arrows: a dense teacher, temperature control, adaptive soft labels, the MoE student with its forward and backward passes, evaluation and reward calculation, a stability filter, router shift calculation and filtered gradients. The right column has EMA advantage, expert frequency, load-balancing bias update and router bias. Dashed arrows labeled Updated Router Bias and Updated Experts loop back along the top and bottom. A legend explains solid versus dashed arrows.
caption: Path-Aligned Decompression Distillation (PADD) framework overview. PADD organizes dense-to-MoE knowledge distillation into four stages: Stage I performs neuron clustering and expert initialization, while Stages II--IV integrate online adaptive distillation, path-refined policy optimization, and reward-augmented load balancing in a unified training pipeline.
abstract: As large language models (LLMs) continue to scale, it becomes increasingly challenging to grow model capacity under fixed computation budgets. We propose Path-Aligned Decompression Distillation (PADD), a framework for distilling knowledge from dense teachers without explicit routing into mixture-of-experts (MoE) students while learning high-quality routing policies. PADD organizes knowledge distillation into four stages in two phases: an initialization phase (Stage I) that builds diverse functionality in the student's experts through teacher neuron clustering and student-expert warmup, and a training phase (Stages II--IV) that integrates online adaptive distillation, path-refined policy optimization, and reward-augmented load balancing in a single training pipeline. Experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that PADD yields substantial gains over strong baselines at the same inference cost and that the MoE student can match or surpass its dense teacher. They also demonstrate effective teacher-to-student knowledge distillation and stable routing behavior.
